items.stem: A quality engineer sees points varying within the control limits with no pattern. This indicates:

options.text: Common-cause variation inherent to the process
options.rationale: Correct: in-control variation with no pattern is common cause.

options.text: A special cause requiring immediate reaction
options.rationale: No signal means no special cause to chase.
Normal variation does not mean a broken chart.
In-control status does not call for stopping monitoring.

items.explanation: Correct: in-control variation with no pattern is common cause.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: For a recurring defect, the most effective quality action is to:

options.text: Perform root-cause analysis and address the underlying cause
options.rationale: Correct: solving the root cause prevents recurrence.
More inspection does not remove the cause.

options.text: Ignore it if customers have not complained

options.rationale: Blame without analysis misses the cause.

items.explanation: Correct: solving the root cause prevents recurrence.

items.stem: Select TWO categories in the cost of quality.

options.rationale: Correct: prevention is a cost-of-quality category.
Correct: internal and external failure are cost-of-quality categories.
Travel is not a cost-of-quality category.
Rent is overhead, not cost of quality.
Bonuses are not a cost-of-quality category.

items.explanation: Correct: prevention is a cost-of-quality category. Correct: internal and external failure are cost-of-quality categories.
